findings.title: Recut body flips SECURITY INVOKER -> SECURITY DEFINER, a literal departure from the house rule that a recut body preserves its SECURITY posture
findings.summary: The house migration law (restated in the review brief) is that a recut body keeps its owner, SECURITY mode, search_path and ACL. 0320 recuts clara.get_client_financial_pack (originally `security invoker` in 0232:862) as `security definer` (0320:999). search_path (`clara, pg_temp`) and the ACL (clara_authenticated) are verifiably unchanged; only the SECURITY mode moves.
findings.evidence: 0232 (packages/db/migrations/0232_client_financial_pack.sql:857-863): `create function clara.get_client_financial_pack(...) language plpgsql stable security invoker set search_path = clara, pg_temp`. 0320 (packages/db/migrations/0320_client_financial_pack_wake_read.sql:988-999): the file's own comment block says "SECURITY INVOKER -> SECURITY DEFINER, and the reason is the one-ungranted-core law rather than a widening", then `create or replace function clara.get_client_financial_pack(...) language plpgsql stable security definer set search_path = clara, pg_temp`. This is a genuine, deliberate change to a previously-shipped human-facing door's trust boundary, not an accident: the migration cites the 0082 precedent by name, and §TAIL reverses the three anchored edits (including the floor-check swap that the SECURITY change necessitates) and hashes the result back to the pinned 0232 pre-image, and a vacuity control (removing `and cl.firm_id = p_firm`) was run and caught by both p1000.wake.no_oracle and the human lane's own p660.pack.cross_firm cell. The change is well-reasoned and well-proven, but the review brief's own house-law phrasing ("SECURITY DEFINER ... preserved on recut bodies") is not literally true of this migration, and a caller who trusts that phrasing at face value (e.g. skimming migrations for security-posture drift) would miss this one because it announces itself as a recut rather than a posture change.
findings.required_fix: No code change needed if the orchestrator accepts the in-file justification (it is thorough and matches an established estate precedent, 0082). Recommend the orchestrator explicitly sign off on this one departure in the cut report or PR description, since it is a security-relevant exception to a documented default rather than a bug.
